G — Sign / provenance: commit-before-draw receipt + tamper test

Letter folder G_provenance/ of the Quantum Phantoms reverse-engineering epic (epic). Markdown is the source of truth; python -m shared.site.build renders it to site/G_provenance/index.html. Target states live only in status.json (lifecycle: listed → dissected → reproduced → adapted → integrated | rejected).

Purpose

Commit rulebook + code hash before the job; fill the receipt (job IDs, counts, S/H_min, witnesses, params, seed, code hash); sign with Ed25519; append to a hash-chained ledger (format modelled on C's beacon chain) and a DICOM tag. A CT-GAN-style injection/removal must fail verification. Pitched as traceability, not security.

How to run (sim commands)

Working directory reverse-engineering/. G runs no quantum job; every number it reports comes from files other letters made. Runs go to G_provenance/runs/ (gitignored: keys, the ledger, series that may hold LIDC voxels).

python -m G_provenance.src.keys init                       # once: demo Ed25519 key + trusted_keys.json
python -m G_provenance.src.receipt commit                  # BEFORE the job: prints "committed: ledger index i"
# ... run C (certify), E / F, as usual ...
python -m G_provenance.src.receipt fill --commit G_provenance/runs/<ts>-commit/receipt.json \
    [--certificate .../certificate.json --job .../quantum_job_record.json --hybrid .../hybrid_volume.json ...]
python -m G_provenance.src.dicom_export G_provenance/runs/<ts>-fill/receipt.json   # CT series with provenance tags
python -m G_provenance.src.verify G_provenance/runs/<ts>-dicom/series              # VERIFIED / TAMPER DETECTED: ...
python -m G_provenance.repro.r19_ctgan_tamper --n 20       # target #19: tamper test, table + figures

Inputs not given default to shared/stubs/ (exempt from the order and code checks, recorded in fill_report.json). A certificate with status: "fail" signs nothing ("certificate failed, nothing to sign", exit 0). Any failed check (order, producer code hash, rulebook hash) writes fill_report.json, signs nothing and exits 1.

Reproduced result vs. paper

Target #19 (G01 §7.2: sign each scan to detect CT-GAN tampering). The GAN is replaced by a classical in-painter; everything else in the pre/post-processing follows the paper (see the dossier).

paper ours (stub phantom, n = 20 per kind)
injection / removal detected by the signature qualitative claim 20 / 20 and 20 / 20, failing check voxels, slice Jaccard 1.00
forgeries: seed edit / re-sign / ledger rewrite / commit deletion — caught by signature / trusted_key / trusted_key only / commit_first
controls (untampered, unbound tag re-saved) — 0 false positives
readers misdiagnose 99 % (injected) and 94 % (removed); AI 100 % measured not reproduced (needs radiologists and the trained GAN; H's territory)

Figures: figures/r19-ctgan-tamper.png, figures/r19-detection-table.png.

Claim level and honesty notes

Provenance layer (claim level n/a, no quantum claim). Everything after the quantum job must be deterministic and replayable from the receipt.

  • Traceability, not security. The tamper test checks that data still matches what was committed and signed.
  • Demo key, not a PKI. One random Ed25519 key per machine, pinned in trusted_keys.json. The stub key is never trusted.
  • Limit (attack c). A forger who holds the trusted key and rewrites the ledger end to end cannot be detected from the files alone; only the pinned key stops it. Future fix: anchor the ledger head in a public beacon pulse (C dossier #5).
  • Order is proved by ledger index + created_utc, with one-second resolution; stub inputs are exempt and flagged.
  • Simulated upstream numbers keep their sim_label inside the files the receipt references; G does not restate them as hardware results.
  • No GAN was trained or run; the in-painter is classical, so stealth against human readers is not claimed.

Pipeline readiness

Prototype

G blocks the chain. receipt fill --job takes one value, the chain passes five quantum job records (C, B, 3× D), and argparse keeps only the last (D's QCA job), so C's, B's and two of D's jobs are not bound into the receipt (probe runs/20261029-185947-probe-gaps: the only block). The commit ran in all four prefix chains, but its ledger entry says kind: "receipt" (CCR-G1), and its code hash freezes the .py files of A–F only. G and H code and the parameter JSONs can change after the commit. The verifier itself catches every edit in R19 (20 / 20); keys are a per-machine demo key with no PKI.

Future

Shared, pipeline-wide context (end goal, digital-twin path, cross-letter risks) lives once in the whole-pipeline Future. This section covers only what this letter adds. Every claim carries a label: evidence-based (a number in this repo or a cited paper), extrapolation (a reasoned step beyond the evidence), speculative (possible, not supported yet).

1. Aim of the paper(s)

  • [G01] Mirsky et al. (CT-GAN): shows that an attacker can inject or remove lung tumours in 3-D CT with a generative model, fooling both radiologists and AI, and proposes digitally signing scans as a defence.

Why it matters: synthetic medical images are only useful as evidence if anyone can check where they came from and that nothing changed since.

2. Contribution

  • Commit before draw: rulebook + code hashes are signed and ledgered before the quantum job, so nothing can be tuned after seeing the result. evidence-based
  • An Ed25519 receipt, a hash-chained ledger and a DICOM private tag. Injection and removal are detected 20/20 each, with 0 false positives. evidence-based
  • INT findings: the commit freezes only A–F .py code, and fill --job binds 1 of 5 jobs. evidence-based

3. Role in cancer detection

End goal: every synthetic case used to train or test a cancer detector is traceable to its rulebook, code version, quantum job and seed, and an auditor can replay it. A detector's validation set can then be proven unchanged since it was committed. This is credibility, not security. extrapolation

4. Beyond lungs

  • Any synthetic medical data (MR, pathology, genomics), and virtual clinical trials, where regulators ask for traceable in-silico evidence [G02]. extrapolation
  • Real-data lineage. The same receipts can document preprocessing of real scans used for AI training. extrapolation

5. Long-term vision: toward a digital twin

speculative A twin that informs decisions must be auditable: which model version, which data and which random inputs produced a forecast. Path: (1) receipts for synthetic tumours (now) → (2) receipts for every pipeline run, anchored in a public beacon → (3) a provenance layer under every twin simulation, so any forecast can be replayed bit-for-bit.

6. Predictions

5 years Assumptions: demo keys; a local ledger.

  • Verification catches every voxel edit in the R19 setting. evidence-based
  • The ledger head is anchored in public beacon pulses, and parameter JSONs are frozen in the commit. extrapolation

10 years Assumptions: institutional PKI / HSM keys; standards for synthetic-data provenance.

  • Receipts travel inside DICOM as an accepted provenance record for research datasets. extrapolation

15 years Assumptions: fault-tolerant quantum hardware exists.

  • speculative Shor's algorithm on such hardware breaks elliptic-curve signatures, Ed25519 included. Receipts must migrate to post-quantum signatures well before then, and old ledgers need re-anchoring. This is the one place where fault tolerance is a threat to the pipeline rather than an opportunity.
